canada.title: Oil trading in triple digits, but Canadian crude selling at steeper discount
canada.summary: Canadian oil is typically sold at a discount compared to the North American benchmark, but that gap has widened in recent months with no clear short-term solution in sight.

canada.title: Parents of boy who died from CO poisoning say his legacy lives on as new Sask. law comes into effect
canada.summary: Marina Hills and Sergio Losco are working to keep their son Henry's legacy alive as a law named after him is set to come into effect in Saskatchewan on Nov. 1. The 11-year-old died as a result of a carbon monoxide leak after a boiler malfunction in the Metro 1827 apartment building in downtown Regina last December.

canada.title: Saskatoon city hall reviews procedures in wake of too-tall house dilemma
canada.summary: The owners of a home on University Drive in the Nutana neighbourhood are appealing — for the second time — an order to halt work on the nearly completed house after an inspection in May found the structure exceeded the maximum height allowed.

canada.title: Akaitcho First Nations want to see action on long medical travel
canada.summary: The concerns discussed on Tuesday at the Akaitcho Territory Government's annual general assembly include medical travel, high cancer rates, housing and the spread of drugs and alcohol in their communities. Chiefs and delegates shared stories, personal or previously shared with them, of bad experiences on the long medical travel flight from Yellowknife to Edmonton.

canada.title: Whitehorse man arrested after incidents targeting mosque faces new hate-related charge
canada.summary: James Joseph Thomas faces a new charge of committing an offence motivated by hatred based on religion — namely, mischief — after an Islamophobic message was spray-painted onto a building downtown on Sept. 21.

canada.title: Manitobans head to polls today for general municipal election
canada.summary: Today is municipal election day for most of Manitoba. Voting locations will be open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m.

canada.title: Ontario pauses some skills training funding for unemployed people: career colleges
canada.summary: In addition to freezing Ontario Student Assistance Program payments to all private post-secondary institutions, the province has paused at least some funding through Better Jobs Ontario. But the government won’t explicitly say so.

canada.title: N.B. government's public opinion survey on fracking is biased, critics say
canada.summary: Critics of fracking say a public survey that is part of the New Brunswick government’s review of the fracking moratorium is biased, and some are calling for an independent, third-party review.

canada.title: PC leader calls Liberal cuts to oversight committee hours ‘Trumpish’
canada.summary: The opposition Progressive Conservatives are urging the Holt government to reverse course on a planned reduction in sitting days for a key committee that is supposed to monitor the spending of taxpayer dollars.

canada.title: Premier's office criticizes professor over comments on proposed N.S. data centre
canada.summary: Sibo Chen of Toronto Metropolitan University, formerly Ryerson University, has been writing critically about the environmental impacts of resource extraction and AI growth, but said it's the first time he has received a complaint from a premier's office about his viewpoints.

canada.title: Worries run high, tanks run low more than 2 weeks into Bell Island fuel shortage
canada.summary: Bell Island’s only gas station has been without fuel for more than two weeks, leaving some residents frustrated and stuck in place.

canada.title: More than half of N.L.'s Parks Canada workers at risk of losing their jobs
canada.summary: As the federal government agency launches a workforce adjustment exercise thanks to budget cuts, more than half of Parks Canada employees in Newfoundland and Labrador have been told they could lose their jobs.

canada.title: 10 students suspended at Lévis, Que., high school for posting AI-altered images of staff
canada.summary: Ten students at a high school in Lévis, Que., have been suspended after several AI-altered images of teachers and school staff were posted to Snapchat. Experts say both teachers and students need more education about the risks of AI and online images.

canada.title: Rise of makeshift shelters raises safety concerns as winter nears in Montreal
canada.summary: Pallets, tarps, ropes, bits of insulation and a dash of ingenuity — an increasing number of unhoused Montrealers are cobbling together makeshift shelters, prompting the city to take a closer look at the trend as winter approaches.
